XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT

The P.S.I., of Marathahalli Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused No.1 & 2 for the offence punishable under sections Secs.498A, 323, 506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC and Secs.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
2.
BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :

It is the case of the complainant that, she got married with accused No.1 as per Hindu rites and customs at Sri.Lakshmi Narayana Temple Munnekollal in the presence of the elders, at the time of marriage as per the say of the accused No.1 to 4, CW.4 & 5 have given 35 Sovereign gold, 15 KG Silver ornaments, one Car as dowry and performed the marriage of the CW.1 by spending Rs.13,00,000/-.

It is further alleged that, the complainant went to her matrimonial house and led happy marital life for two months and thereafter, the C.C.No.50457/2022 accused persons subjected CW.1 to the cruelty, accused No.1 demanded dowry of Rs.5,00,000/- and subjected her to cruelty by harassing her both physically and mentally.

It is further alleged that, from Sharika Sushma H vs Lokesh D on 1 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120437884/
2 the month of June 2021, the complainant was residing with accused No.1 at the house No.70/1-2, which is rented house and CW.2 and 3 have purchased the house hold articles and given to the CW.1.

sentences.text: It is further alleged that, the accused No.4 misbehaved to the complainant, accused No.1 and 4 have assaulted CW.1 with hands and also threatened CW.1 with dire consequences.

Based on the typed complaint lodged by C.W.1, police authorities have registered the case against accused No.1 to 4 in P.S.
Crime No.235/2021 for the offence punishable under sections 498(a), 323, 506 R/w 34 of IPC and section 3 & 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Investigating Officers after completion of the investigation has submitted final report against the accused No.1 to 4 for the above said offences.
3. Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above mentioned offence alleged against the accused No.1 to 4 and registered the criminal case against them.
. During the crime stage, the accused No.1 to 4 have obtained anticipatory bail and have been released on bail by this court.
After registering the case, the accused No.1 to 4 have appeared.
Copy of the final report and it's enclosures were furnished to them in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
During the course of the trial, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has quashed the proceedings against accused No.2 and 3 vide dated 05.07.2023 in Crl.Pet.No.3158/2022.
Sufficient grounds were made out to frame charges.
Hence, charges framed and read over to the accused No.1 and 4 only.

They pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.
5.

In order to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 & 4, the prosecution has examined two witnesses out of 15 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 and PW.2 and relied upon documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 and closed its side.
In lieu of absence of incriminating circumstances appearing against accused No.1 and 4, recording of their statement under section 313 of Cr.P.C. was dispensed with.
6. Heard both sides.
Perused the materials on record.

7. The points that arise for my consideration are;
C.C.No.50457/2022 1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that the accused No.1 was married with CW.1 on 30.08.2020 and thereafter, the accused No.1 has subjected CW.1 to cruelty by harassing her both by physically and mentally and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.498A of IPC ?

2. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused No.1 has demanded dowry of Rs.5,00,000/- from CW.1 and subjected her to cruelty and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act ?

sentences.text:
3. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all in furtherance of common intention have assaulted CW.1 with hands and caused simple injuries and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.323 R/w 34 of IPC ?
4. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all in furtherance of common intention have C.C.No.50457/2022 threatened CW.1 with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.506 R/w 34 of IPC ?
5. What Order?
8. My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point Nos.1 to 4 : In the Negative.
Point No.5 :

In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 and 4, the prosecution has examined the complainant/victim/C.W.1 as P.W.1, the mother of the complainant/CW.5 as PW.2 and relied upon ten documents.

10. In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 and 4, the prosecution has examined the complainant / victim CW.1 as PW.1, wherein, the said witness has not supported the case of the prosecution.

The learned APP C.C.No.50457/2022 appearing for the State with permission treated the said witness as hostile and fully cross examined her, wherein, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of the PW.1 in order to prove the guilt of the accused No.1 and 4.
11.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused No.1 and 4, the prosecution has examined the mother of the complainant/CW.5 as PW.2, wherein, she has not supported the case of the prosecution.
Nothing was elicited from her mouth during the cross examination by the learned APP in order to prove the contents of her statement given before the police.
12. On perusal of the materials on record and the oral & documentary evidence of P.W.1 and 2, they have categorically admitted that, they have compromised the matter with the accused Nos.1 and 4.

In view of the evidence of P.W.1 and 4, since the matter was compromised, the prayer of the learned Senior Asst. Public Prosecutor for issuance of witness summons to other witnesses was rejected as no purpose would be served.

As the P.W.1 and 2 have turned hostile to the case of the prosecution,
the evidence on record is not at all helpful to substantiate the guilt of the accused No.1 and 4.

Hence,
there is no cogent and convincing evidence C.C.No.50457/2022 against the accused No.1 and 4.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the benefit of doubt has to be extended to the accused No.1 and 4 and hence, the Point Nos.1 to 4 are answered in the "Negative".

13. Point No.5 :- In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.1 and 4 are acquitted of the offence punishable under Secs.498A, 323, 506 R/w Sec.34 of IPC and Secs.3 & 4 of D.P.Act.
The Bail bonds and Surety Bonds of the accused No.1 & 4 shall be in force for the period of 6 months and thereafter it shall be cancelled without further orders.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and typed by her, corrected by me and then signed and pronounced in the Open Court on this date the 01 st day of February, 2025.)
